title: SYNC 2/SYNC 3: Finding the Entertainment Components
introduction:
I use this illustration as the audio system's backstage map. The display, SYNC electronics, microphones and speakers have separate jobs and separate locations; the screen is only the part taking the bow.

Start with the component description in the table, find its matching numbered inset, then follow the leader line to the location dot on the car. The small inset shows the component's appearance; the dot places it in the vehicle. The drawing combines equipment alternatives, so match the coupe or convertible body style, Shaker equipment and optional satellite-radio qualifiers before choosing a row. Front antenna-cable entries marked “Not shown” have no plotted location.

The APIM is the accessory protocol interface module that handles SYNC connected-device, voice and media functions. ACM identifies the audio front control module, FDIM the front display interface module, GPSM the global positioning system module, and DSP the audio digital signal processing module. For location abbreviations, LH and RH mean left-hand and right-hand, while F and R identify front and rear.

Use this reference to identify a component and its general location. The table retains the exact equipment distinctions and identifiers. The illustration provides neither a trim-removal route nor connector orientation, pin assignments or electrical test instructions.

edits.text: ANC (active noise control) microphones apply to 2.3L vehicles only. On a coupe, they are in the overhead console and at the center rear of the headliner. On a convertible, they are in the overhead console, the RHR quarter panel and the LHR quarter panel.
edits.why: Body style changes where these microphones are located. I match that qualifier before following the illustration, keeping the ANC microphones distinct from the separately identified SYNC microphone.
